title: Three-step calc lower-bounding |ζ(3)/ζ(3/2)| by |ζ(3/2 + it)| via the Euler product
intent: Prove the lower bound |ζ(3/2 + it)| ≥ |ζ(3)/ζ(3/2)| on the critical line by factoring it into a three-link calc: evaluate the ratio ζ(3)/ζ(3/2) as a real Euler product (abs_zeta_ratio_eval), compare that product factorwise to the product of inverse norms of the Euler factors at 3/2 + it (abs_zeta_inequality), then fold that product back into |ζ(3/2 + it)| (abs_zeta_prod_prime).

parent.name: zeta_lower_bound
parent.statement:
theorem zeta_lower_bound (t : ℝ) :
  norm (riemannZeta 3 / riemannZeta ((3 : ℝ) / 2)) ≤
    norm (riemannZeta (((3 : ℝ) / 2) + t * Complex.I))

children.name: abs_zeta_ratio_eval
children.statement: lemma abs_zeta_ratio_eval : norm (riemannZeta 3 / riemannZeta ((3 : ℝ) / 2)) = ∏' p : ℙ, (1 + ((p : ℕ) : ℝ) ^ (-((3 : ℝ) / 2)))⁻¹
children.closed_by: 4-link calc: h_abs_ratio (congrArg norm applied to zeta_ratio_at_3_2), h_abs_tprod (abs_of_tprod w hw_mult), simp [h_abs_eq_fun], then rfl — with multipliable_positive_inv_powers and Complex.ofReal_cpow carrying the complex↔real factor identification

children.name: abs_zeta_inequality
children.statement:
lemma abs_zeta_inequality (t : ℝ) :
  ∏' p : ℙ, (1 + ((p : ℕ) : ℝ) ^ (-((3 : ℝ) / 2)))⁻¹ ≤
  ∏' p : ℙ, (norm (1 - ((p : ℕ) : ℂ) ^ (-(((3 : ℝ) / 2) + t * Complex.I))))⁻¹
children.closed_by: convert both products to NNReal (multipliable_real_to_nnreal), apply prod_inequality f g hf hg h_pointwise with h_pointwise = abs_term_inv_bound p t (per-prime), convert back with nnreal_tprod_le_coe; multipliability from multipliable_positive_inv_powers and multipliable_complex_abs_inv (via zetaEulerprod)

children.name: abs_zeta_prod_prime
children.statement:
lemma abs_zeta_prod_prime (s : ℂ) (hs : 1 < s.re) :
  norm (riemannZeta s) = ∏' p : ℙ, (norm (1 - ((p : ℕ) : ℂ) ^ (-s : ℂ)))⁻¹
children.closed_by: rw [abs_zeta_prod s hs]; congr 1; ext p; rw [abs_of_inv (1 - ((p : ℕ) : ℂ) ^ (-s : ℂ)) (one_minus_p_s_neq_0 p s hs)]

applicability.goal_shape: A real bound A ≤ B where A is a concrete analytic value (here norm (ζ(3)/ζ(3/2))) and B is norm (ζ(s)) for s on a line (here 3/2 + it); the middle term is an Euler product over primes, and the proof is a single = ≤ = calc.
applicability.use_when: both endpoints admit an Euler-product (or analogous) rewrite as an infinite product over the same index set; the factorwise comparison (one ≤ link) and the two product rewrites (one = link each) can each be stated as a self-contained named lemma; the middle terms definitionally match the adjacent links so `calc` joins them.
applicability.avoid_when: the two product rewrites are one-line rw/simp steps (inline them rather than name lemmas); the factorwise bound needs too much local context to be a clean standalone statement; the two products are indexed by different sets, so no single middle term joins the chain.

consequences: The move creates three obligations, one per link: (a) evaluate the concrete value to a product (abs_zeta_ratio_eval); (b) a factorwise bound between two products, carrying a multipliability/summability obligation for both sides (abs_zeta_inequality); (c) fold the product back into a function value, carrying the side condition 1 < Re s (abs_zeta_prod_prime, fed by the parent's `have hs`). Failure modes: the side condition hs must be discharged by the parent (here simp/norm_num) before link 3 elaborates; the factorwise step is the analytic heart and its NNReal multipliability hypotheses are heavy, so a child whose statement drifts from the chain endpoints will not elaborate; and if the two product rewrites were not already available as named lemmas, they would have to be stated first or inlined.
